Yesterday
what is perceptron vs human brain
Short answer:  
A perceptron is a very simple mathematical model of a neuron.
The human brain is a massively complex biological system with billions of adaptive, interconnected neurons.
They are not comparable in power — the perceptron is only loosely inspired by the brain.

Below is a clear, structured comparison grounded in the sources you saw.

🧠 What a Perceptron Is
A perceptron is an artificial neuron used in machine learning. It takes inputs, multiplies them by weights, sums them, applies an activation function, and outputs a decision.
This is a simplified digital model designed to mimic only the very basic behavior of a biological neuron.

Key characteristics:

Inputs → weighted sum → activation → output

Learns by adjusting weights

Performs simple, rule‑based learning

Structure is fixed and simple

🧬 What a Human Neuron/Brain Is
A biological neuron is a living cell with dendrites, soma, axon, and synapses.
It processes electrochemical signals, forms new connections, rewires itself, and participates in extremely complex networks.

Key characteristics:

86 billion neurons in the brain

Each neuron connects to thousands of others

Learns through synaptic plasticity

Can reorganize, adapt, and self‑repair

Biological neurons are far more computationally powerful than perceptrons — even a single neuron can perform complex nonlinear operations.

🔍 Side‑by‑Side Comparison
Feature	Perceptron (Artificial Neuron)	Human Brain / Biological Neuron
Nature	Mathematical model	Living biological cell
Structure	Inputs, weights, activation	Dendrites, soma, axon, synapses
Learning	Adjusts weights using math rules	Forms/strengthens/rewires synapses
Complexity	Very simple	Extremely complex electrochemical processes
Connections	Few	Up to 10,000+ per neuron
Adaptability	Low	Very high (neuroplasticity)
Energy use	High (computers consume a lot)	Brain runs on ~20 watts
Function	Linear/nonlinear classification	Reasoning, memory, emotion, creativity
Origin	Inspired by neurons but diverged	Product of evolution


🎯 The Core Difference
A perceptron is not a realistic model of a human neuron.
It is a simplified abstraction created to make neural networks possible.
Biological neurons are far more powerful, dynamic, and complex than anything in artificial neural networks.

🚀 Summary
Perceptron = simple digital switch

Human neuron = complex biological processor

Brain = massive adaptive network with trillions of connections

AI is inspired by the brain, but the similarity ends at the surface level

You’re diving into a great topic, sibtain — and the image you shared perfectly sets the stage.
Let me give you a clear, sharp, professional explanation of Perceptron vs Human Brain, using the diagram as context but explaining it in a deeper, more intuitive way.

🧠 Perceptron vs Human Brain — The Real Difference
⭐ 1. What a Perceptron Actually Is
A perceptron is the simplest possible artificial neuron.
It does exactly what your diagram shows:

Takes inputs

Multiplies them by weights

Adds a bias

Applies an activation function

Produces a binary output (0 or 1)

It’s basically a mathematical decision unit.

Think of it like:
A calculator that checks:
“Is the weighted sum ≥ 0? If yes → output 1, else → output 0.”

That’s it.

⭐ 2. What a Human Neuron Does
A biological neuron is not a simple switch.
It is a living, adaptive, electrochemical processor.

A single neuron can:

Integrate thousands of signals

Fire in complex patterns

Strengthen or weaken connections

Grow new synapses

Change its structure

Communicate using chemicals, not just electricity

Participate in memory, emotion, reasoning, creativity

A human brain has:

86 billion neurons

100 trillion synaptic connections

Dynamic rewiring every second

Energy efficiency of ~20 watts

This is far beyond anything in artificial neural networks.

🔍 Side‑by‑Side Comparison (Clear & Practical)
Feature	Perceptron	Human Neuron / Brain
Type	Mathematical model	Biological cell
Inputs	Few	Thousands
Learning	Adjust weights	Synaptic plasticity, rewiring
Output	Binary (0/1)	Complex firing patterns
Adaptability	Low	Extremely high
Energy use	High (computers)	Very low (20W brain)
Function	Simple classification	Thinking, memory, emotion, creativity
Scale	Dozens → millions	86 billion neurons


🎯 The Core Truth
A perceptron is not a realistic model of a human neuron.
It is only inspired by the brain — like a stick figure inspired by a real human.

AI ≠ Brain
Perceptron ≠ Neuron
Neural networks ≠ Biological networks

They share the idea of weighted inputs → output, but the similarity ends there.

🧱 Core idea: What is a CodeableConcept (in DB terms)?
A CodeableConcept usually represents:

A concept (like diagnosis, procedure, service, specialty, etc.)

With one or more codings (e.g., NPHIES code, SNOMED, ICD, internal code)

Plus human‑readable text

So in database design, you normally separate:

CodeableConcept (the logical concept)

Coding (each individual code system entry)

🗂 Suggested table structure
1. CodeableConcept table
CodeableConceptID (PK)

DisplayText – human readable text (e.g., “Appendectomy”)

CategoryType – e.g., Diagnosis, Procedure, Service, Drug, etc.

IsActive – flag

CreatedOn / UpdatedOn

2. Coding table
Each row = one code in one system for one concept.

CodingID (PK)

CodeableConceptID (FK → CodeableConcept)

System – e.g., http://nphies.sa/CodeSystem/...

Version – NPHIES version (e.g., 2.6)

Code – actual code value

Display – system’s display text

IsPrimary – is this the main code for the concept?

IsActive

EffectiveFrom / EffectiveTo

3. Optional: CodeableConceptUsage table
If NPHIES sheets show different contexts (e.g., claim, invoice, authorization, encounter), you can model:

UsageID (PK)

CodeableConceptID (FK)

UsageContext – e.g., Claim.Diagnosis, Claim.Item.Service, Encounter.Type

RequiredFlag – Required / Optional / Conditional

ValidationRuleID – link to validation rules

Path (Element)

Definition

VS URL

So the table becomes:

Columns:

ProfileID (PK)

PathElement

Definition

This table tells you:

“At this FHIR path, use this ValueSet.”

Example:
Claim.item.productOrService → must use ValueSet X.

🧠 2. How These Tables Work Together
✔ CodeSystem → defines codes
✔ ValueSet → selects which codes are allowed
✔ Profile → tells NPHIES where to apply the ValueSet
This is exactly how FHIR/NPHIES validation works.

🔗 3. How to Use This in Your Claim System
When validating a claim:

Identify the FHIR path (e.g., Claim.item.productOrService)

Look up the Profile table → find the ValueSet

Look up the ValueSet → find allowed CodeSystems

Look up CodeSystemCodes → check if the code is valid

This matches NPHIES validation rules.

🟩 PART 4 — HOW NPHIES VALIDATION WORKS USING THIS DB
When validating a claim field (e.g., Claim.item.productOrService):

From your Profiles sheet (Path → ValueSet)

From ValueSet_CodeSystem_Map

From CodeSystemCode

From ValueSet_Code_Filter

Step 5 — Validate the submitted code

⭐ THE FINAL NPHIES TERMINOLOGY DATABASE DESIGN
This is the only design you need.
It supports all the appendices you gave me:

RTA diagnosis

Cause of death

Route of administration

Specialty

Benefit category

Benefit type

Body site

FDI tooth region

Imaging / lab / procedures / devices

And all HL7/NPHIES CodeSystems

Everything fits into 5 core tables.

🟦 1. CodeSystem
Stores metadata for each CodeSystem.

Columns:
CodeSystemID (PK)

CS_URL

CS_Version

CS_Name

CS_Title

CS_Description

CS_Committee

CS_OID

CS_Copyright

CS_SourceResource

IsActive

Example:
Code

http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/cause-of-death
http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/route-of-admin
🟩 2. CodeSystemCode
Stores the actual codes inside each CodeSystem.

Columns:
CodeID (PK)

CodeSystemID (FK → CodeSystem)

Code

Display

Definition

IsActive

AppendixReference (optional)

Example:
Code
V00.10 | Ped vs pdcnv trf acdt unspec | rta-diagnosis
EBPROA0009 | EPIDURAL | route-of-admin
01.00 | Anesthesiology Specialty | practice-codes
This table will contain tens of thousands of rows — and that’s correct.

🟧 3. ValueSet
Stores metadata for each ValueSet.

Columns:
ValueSetID (PK)

VS_URL

VS_Version

VS_Name

VS_Title

VS_Definition

VS_Committee

VS_Identifier

VS_Restrictions

VS_SourceResource

IsActive

Example:
Code
http://nphies.sa/terminology/ValueSet/rta-diagnosis
http://nphies.sa/terminology/ValueSet/cause-of-death
http://nphies.sa/terminology/ValueSet/route-of-admin
🟨 4. ValueSet_CodeSystem_Map
Links each ValueSet to the CodeSystems it uses.

Columns:
VS_CS_MapID (PK)

ValueSetID (FK → ValueSet)

CodeSystemID (FK → CodeSystem)

CS_URL_Validation (optional)

Example:

  - imaging
  - laboratory
  - medical-devices
  - oral-health-ip
  - oral-health-op
  - services
  - medication-codes
This table supports 1-to-many and many-to-many relationships.

🟫 5. ValueSet_Code_Filter (optional but recommended)
Used when a ValueSet restricts codes (e.g., (PRC, PPN, NI, VP, MR)).

Columns:
VS_FilterID (PK)

ValueSetID (FK)

Code

Notes

All CodeSystems

🧠 HOW VALIDATION WORKS USING THIS DATABASE
Example: Validate Claim.item.productOrService
Find the FHIR path → Claim.item.productOrService

Look up the ValueSet for that path

Load all CodeSystems linked to that ValueSet

Load all codes from those CodeSystems

Check if the submitted code exists

Check if it is active

Check if it belongs to the correct CodeSystem

Check if it is allowed in the ValueSet

This is exactly how NPHIES validation engines work.

You’ve basically built the terminology layer of nphies—nice work collecting all that. Let’s turn it into a clean, future‑proof schema.

1. Core SQL schema (metadata + concepts)
1.1. Code system metadata
sql
CREATE TABLE CodeSystem (
    CodeSystemId      INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    Url               NVARCHAR(300)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Version           NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
    Name              NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
    Title             NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    Definition        NVARCHAR(MAX)  NULL,
    Committee         NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
    Oid               NVARCHAR(100)  NULL,
    Copyright         NVARCHAR(MAX)  NULL,
    SourceResource    NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    CreatedAt         DATETIME2      NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME()
);
1.2. Value set metadata
sql
CREATE TABLE ValueSet (
    ValueSetId        INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    Url               NVARCHAR(300)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    Version           NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
    Name              NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
    Title             NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    Definition        NVARCHAR(MAX)  NULL,
    Committee         NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
    Oid               NVARCHAR(100)  NULL,
    Copyright         NVARCHAR(MAX)  NULL,
    SourceResource    NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    CreatedAt         DATETIME2      NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME()
);
1.3. Value set ↔ code system link
sql
CREATE TABLE ValueSetCodeSystem (
    ValueSetId     INT NOT NULL,
    CodeSystemId   INT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (ValueSetId, CodeSystemId),
    CONSTRAINT FK_ValueSetCodeSystem_ValueSet
        FOREIGN KEY (ValueSetId) REFERENCES ValueSet(ValueSetId),
    CONSTRAINT FK_ValueSetCodeSystem_CodeSystem
        FOREIGN KEY (CodeSystemId) REFERENCES CodeSystem(CodeSystemId)
);
1.4. Profile metadata (paths + bindings)
sql
CREATE TABLE Profile (
    ProfileId        INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    Name             NVARCHAR(200)  NULL,
    Url              NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    Version          NVARCHAR(50)   NULL,
    Title            NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    Definition       NVARCHAR(MAX)  NULL,
    SourceResource   NVARCHAR(300)  NULL,
    CreatedAt        DATETIME2      NOT NULL DEFAULT SYSUTCDATETIME()
);

CREATE TABLE ProfileElement (
    ProfileElementId INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    ProfileId        INT           NOT NULL,
    Path             NVARCHAR(400) NOT NULL,   -- e.g. Claim.diagnosis.type
    Definition       NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL,
    ValueSetUrl      NVARCHAR(300) NULL,
    CONSTRAINT FK_ProfileElement_Profile
        FOREIGN KEY (ProfileId) REFERENCES Profile(ProfileId)
);
1.5. Generic concept table (for all appendices)
All your “Appendix=…” sheets (benefit-category, benefit-type, body-site, fdi-tooth-surface, fdi-oral-region, route-of-admin, RTA diagnosis, rejection-reason, specialty, cause-of-death, adjudication-error, etc.) can live in one normalized table, keyed by CodeSystemId.

sql
CREATE TABLE Concept (
    ConceptId        BIGINT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    CodeSystemId     INT           NOT NULL,
    Code             NVARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    Display          NVARCHAR(500) NULL,
    Definition       NVARCHAR(MAX) NULL,   -- Description / long text
    Extra1           NVARCHAR(500) NULL,   -- for special columns if needed
    Extra2           NVARCHAR(500) NULL,
    IsActive         BIT           NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    SortOrder        INT           NULL,
    CONSTRAINT UQ_Concept_Code UNIQUE (CodeSystemId, Code),
    CONSTRAINT FK_Concept_CodeSystem
        FOREIGN KEY (CodeSystemId) REFERENCES CodeSystem(CodeSystemId)
);
Mapping examples:

benefit-category → CodeSystem URL http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/benefit-category, Code, Display, Description → Definition.

route-of-admin → CodeSystem URL http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/route-of-admin, Code, Display, Definition.

RTA diagnosis → CodeSystem URL http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/rta-diagnosis, Code, Display.

rejection-reason → CodeSystem URL http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/adjudication-reason, Detailed code → Code, Display, Descriptions → Definition.

2. ERD (logical relationships)
In words:

CodeSystem 1‑N Concept  
One code system (e.g. route-of-admin) has many concepts (EBPROA0001, EBPROA0002, …).

ValueSet M‑N CodeSystem  
A value set can include codes from multiple code systems; a code system can be used by many value sets. That’s ValueSetCodeSystem.

Profile 1‑N ProfileElement  
One profile has many elements (paths). Each element may bind to a ValueSet via ValueSetUrl.

ProfileElement → ValueSet (logical)  
You can optionally add a FK if you store ValueSetId instead of URL.

If you want a more explicit binding table:

sql
CREATE TABLE ProfileElementBinding (
    ProfileElementBindingId INT IDENTITY(1,1) PRIMARY KEY,
    ProfileElementId        INT NOT NULL,
    ValueSetId              INT NOT NULL,
    Strength                NVARCHAR(50) NULL, -- required / extensible / preferred
    CONSTRAINT FK_PEB_ProfileElement
        FOREIGN KEY (ProfileElementId) REFERENCES ProfileElement(ProfileElementId),
    CONSTRAINT FK_PEB_ValueSet
        FOREIGN KEY (ValueSetId) REFERENCES ValueSet(ValueSetId)
);
3. Import strategy & sample scripts
Assume you export each appendix sheet as CSV.

3.1. Seed the CodeSystem table
Example for a few of your code systems:

sql
INSERT INTO CodeSystem (Url, Name, Title)
VALUES
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/fdi-tooth-surface', 'fdi-tooth-surface', 'FDI Tooth Surface'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/fdi-oral-region',   'fdi-oral-region',   'FDI Oral Region'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/benefit-category',  'benefit-category',  'Benefit Category'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/benefit-type',      'benefit-type',      'Benefit Type'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/bodysite',          'bodysite',          'Body Site'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/route-of-admin',    'route-of-admin',    'Route of Administration'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/rta-diagnosis',     'rta-diagnosis',     'RTA Diagnosis'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/adjudication-reason','adjudication-reason','Adjudication Reason'),
('http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/practice-codes',    'practice-codes',    'Specialty / Practice Codes');
Get IDs for use in imports:

sql
SELECT CodeSystemId, Url FROM CodeSystem;
3.2. Staging tables per sheet
Example: route-of-admin CSV → staging.

sql
CREATE TABLE Stg_RouteOfAdmin (
    Code        NVARCHAR(100),
    Display     NVARCHAR(500),
    Definition  NVARCHAR(MAX),
    CodeSystem  NVARCHAR(300) NULL
);
Bulk load (SQL Server):

sql
BULK INSERT Stg_RouteOfAdmin
FROM 'C:\nphies\route-of-admin.csv'
WITH (
    FIRSTROW = 2,
    FIELDTERMINATOR = ',',
    ROWTERMINATOR   = '\n',
    CODEPAGE = '65001'
);
Then move into Concept:

sql
DECLARE @RouteOfAdminId INT =
    (SELECT CodeSystemId
     FROM CodeSystem
     WHERE Url = 'http://nphies.sa/terminology/CodeSystem/route-of-admin');

INSERT INTO Concept (CodeSystemId, Code, Display, Definition)
SELECT
    @RouteOfAdminId,
    Code,
    Display,
    Definition
FROM Stg_RouteOfAdmin;
Same pattern for:

Stg_BenefitCategory (Code, Display, Description, CodeSystem)

Stg_BenefitType (Code, Display, Display2, CodeSystem → maybe map second Display to Extra1)

Stg_BodySite (Code, Display, CodeSystem)

Stg_FDIToothSurface (Code, Display, Definition, CodeSystem)

Stg_FDIOralRegion (Code, Description, CodeSystem → Description → Display or Definition)

Stg_RTA_Diagnosis (Code, Display, CodeSystem)

Stg_RejectionReason (DetailedCode, Display, Descriptions, CodeSystem)

Stg_Specialty (Code, Display, CodeSystem)

You just adjust the INSERT mapping per sheet.

3.3. ValueSet and Profile imports
ValueSet:

One CSV with columns: VS URL, VS Version, VS Name, VS Title, VS Definition, VS Committee, VS OID, VS Copyright, VS Source Resource, CS URL(s)

Insert into ValueSet, then parse CS URL(s) (split by ; or ,) and insert into ValueSetCodeSystem.

Profile / ProfileElement:

One CSV with columns: ProfileName, ProfileUrl, Path (Element), Definition, VS URL

Upsert into Profile (by ProfileUrl), then insert ProfileElement rows with ValueSetUrl.

4. How this supports your nphies work
You can validate messages by:

Looking up codes in Concept by CodeSystem.Url + Code.

Checking bindings: ProfileElement.Path + ValueSet → allowed codes (via ValueSetCodeSystem + Concept).

You can add new nphies appendices without schema changes—just insert a new CodeSystem row and import its codes into Concept.

You can version later by adding ValidFrom/ValidTo to Concept and ValueSet.
